requirements.quote: The RST_STREAM frame does not define any flags.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame as defining no flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign RST_STREAM-specific semantics to any flag.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's RST_STREAM flag definitions and handling can be inspected or tested.

requirements.quote:
The RST_STREAM frame fully terminates the referenced stream and
   causes it to enter the "closed" state.  After receiving a RST_STREAM
requirements.condition: When an RST_STREAM frame terminates its referenced stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the referenced stream to the closed state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can observe the stream state after processing RST_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
on a stream, the receiver MUST NOT send additional frames for that
   stream, except for PRIORITY.  However, after sending the RST_STREAM,
requirements.condition: After receiving an RST_STREAM on a stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send additional frames on that stream, except PRIORITY frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frames can be monitored after receipt of RST_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
the sending endpoint MUST be prepared to receive and process
   additional frames sent on the stream that might have been sent by the
   peer prior to the arrival of the RST_STREAM.
requirements.condition: After sending an RST_STREAM, when additional stream frames might have been sent by the peer before the RST_STREAM arrived.
requirements.required_behavior: Remain able to receive and process those additional frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can send in-flight frames after the endpoint sends RST_STREAM and verify that they are processed.

requirements.quote:
RST_STREAM frames MUST be associated with a stream.  If a RST_STREAM
   frame is received with a stream identifier of 0x00, the recipient
   MUST treat this as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the frame with a nonzero stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use stream identifier 0x00 for an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.error_behavior: A received RST_STREAM with stream identifier 0x00 must be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame construction and receipt with stream identifier zero can be tested directly.

requirements.quote:
RST_STREAM frames MUST NOT be sent for a stream in the "idle" state.
   If a RST_STREAM frame identifying an idle stream is received, the
   recipient MUST treat this as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of
   type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When the identified stream is in the idle state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send an RST_STREAM for the idle stream.
requirements.error_behavior: A received RST_STREAM identifying an idle stream must be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can place a stream in the idle state and inspect both outbound behavior and handling of an inbound RST_STREAM.

requirements.quote:
A RST_STREAM frame with a length other than 4 octets MUST be treated
   as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a received RST_STREAM frame has a length other than 4 octets.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame as a connection error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed RST_STREAM lengths can be injected and the resulting error type observed.

requirements.quote:
The SETTINGS frame (type=0x04) conveys configuration parameters that
   affect how endpoints communicate, such as preferences and constraints
   on peer behavior.  The SETTINGS frame is also used to acknowledge the
   receipt of those settings.  Individually, a configuration parameter
   from a SETTINGS frame is referred to as a "setting".
requirements.condition: When encoding or recognizing a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use frame type 0x04 for SETTINGS.
requirements.why_checkable: The numeric frame-type mapping is directly inspectable and testable.

requirements.quote:
A SETTINGS frame MUST be sent by both endpoints at the start of a
   connection and MAY be sent at any other time by either endpoint over
   the lifetime of the connection.  Implementations MUST support all of
   the settings defined by this specification.
requirements.condition: At the start of a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Each endpoint must send a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection startup output can be observed for the required SETTINGS frame.

requirements.quote:
A SETTINGS frame MUST be sent by both endpoints at the start of a
   connection and MAY be sent at any other time by either endpoint over
   the lifetime of the connection.  Implementations MUST support all of
   the settings defined by this specification.
requirements.condition: When processing or emitting settings defined by this specification.
requirements.required_behavior: Support all settings defined by this specification.
requirements.why_checkable: Focused tests can exercise each defined setting and verify implementation support.

requirements.quote:
Each parameter in a SETTINGS frame replaces any existing value for
   that parameter.  Settings are processed in the order in which they
   appear, and a receiver of a SETTINGS frame does not need to maintain
   any state other than the current value of each setting.  Therefore,
   the value of a SETTINGS parameter is the last value that is seen by a
   receiver.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS frame contains a parameter for which a value already exists.
requirements.required_behavior: Replace the existing value with the newly processed value.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can apply successive values and inspect the stored current value.

requirements.quote:
Each parameter in a SETTINGS frame replaces any existing value for
   that parameter.  Settings are processed in the order in which they
   appear, and a receiver of a SETTINGS frame does not need to maintain
   any state other than the current value of each setting.  Therefore,
   the value of a SETTINGS parameter is the last value that is seen by a
   receiver.
requirements.condition: When processing multiple settings in a SETTINGS frame, including repeated identifiers.
requirements.required_behavior: Process settings in appearance order so that the last value seen for each parameter is its current value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain an earlier duplicate value as the current value.
requirements.why_checkable: A SETTINGS frame with repeated identifiers can verify ordered processing and last-value-wins behavior.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS frames are acknowledged by the receiving peer.  To enable
   this, the SETTINGS frame defines the ACK flag:
requirements.condition: When a peer receives a SETTINGS frame requiring acknowledgment.
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge the SETTINGS frame using the defined ACK mechanism.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer's output after receiving SETTINGS can be checked for an acknowledgment.

requirements.quote:
ACK (0x01):  When set, the ACK flag indicates that this frame
      acknowledges receipt and application of the peer's SETTINGS frame.
requirements.condition: When the SETTINGS ACK flag value 0x01 is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the frame as acknowledging receipt and application of the peer's SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The parser's interpretation and acknowledgment state transition can be tested with an ACK SETTINGS frame.

requirements.quote:
When this bit is set, the frame payload of the SETTINGS frame MUST
      be empty.  Receipt of a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set and a
      length field value other than 0 MUST be treated as a connection
      error (Section 5.4.1) of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.  For more
requirements.condition: When the ACK flag is set on a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an empty payload and a length field value of 0.
requirements.error_behavior: Receipt with a nonzero length must be treated as a connection error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: ACK frames with zero and nonzero lengths can be parsed and their outcomes observed.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS frames always apply to a connection, never a single stream.
   The stream identifier for a SETTINGS frame MUST be zero (0x00).  If
   an endpoint receives a SETTINGS frame whose Stream Identifier field
   is anything other than 0x00, the endpoint MUST respond with a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the frame to the connection and set its stream identifier to zero (0x00).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not associate a SETTINGS frame with an individual stream or use a nonzero stream identifier.
requirements.error_behavior: On receipt of a SETTINGS frame with a nonzero Stream Identifier, respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream identifier can be inspected on emitted frames and malformed inbound frames can verify the error response.

requirements.quote:
The SETTINGS frame affects connection state.  A badly formed or
   incomplete SETTINGS frame MUST be treated as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS frame is badly formed or incomplete.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed and truncated SETTINGS frames can be supplied and the error type observed.

requirements.quote:
A SETTINGS frame with a length other than a multiple of 6 octets MUST
   be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS frame length is not a multiple of 6 octets.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a connection error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames with invalid payload lengths can be injected and the connection error verified.

requirements.quote:
The frame payload of a SETTINGS frame consists of zero or more
   settings, each consisting of an unsigned 16-bit setting identifier
   and an unsigned 32-bit value.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a SETTINGS frame payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the payload as zero or more settings, each containing an unsigned 16-bit identifier and an unsigned 32-bit value.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload layout and field widths can be checked against encoded or parsed frames.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a SETTINGS frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Length as 24 bits and Type as the 8-bit fixed value 0x04.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized frame header bit widths and the fixed type value are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Unused Flags (7),
     ACK Flag (1),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the SETTINGS flags field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the flags field as seven unused bits and one ACK flag bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The flags field bit allocation can be checked in serialization and parsing code.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31) = 0,
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a SETTINGS frame stream identifier field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the field as one reserved bit followed by a 31-bit Stream Identifier fixed to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a nonzero 31-bit Stream Identifier for SETTINGS.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized header layout and identifier value can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Setting (48) ...,
   }
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the SETTINGS payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode each repeated Setting entry as 48 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload entry size can be checked in serialized frames.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an individual Setting entry.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Identifier in 16 bits and the Value in 32 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Individual setting field widths are directly testable in wire-format serialization and parsing.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE (0x01):  This setting allows the sender to
      inform the remote endpoint of the maximum size of the compression
      table used to decode field blocks, in units of octets.  The
      encoder can select any size equal to or less than this value by
      using signaling specific to the compression format inside a field
      block (see [COMPRESSION]).  The initial value is 4,096 octets.
requirements.condition: Before a SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE value is received or otherwise applied.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an initial SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE value of 4,096 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial stored setting value can be inspected at connection initialization.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE (0x01):  This setting allows the sender to
      inform the remote endpoint of the maximum size of the compression
      table used to decode field blocks, in units of octets.  The
      encoder can select any size equal to or less than this value by
      using signaling specific to the compression format inside a field
      block (see [COMPRESSION]).  The initial value is 4,096 octets.
requirements.condition: When the encoder selects the compression table size after receiving SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE (0x01).
requirements.required_behavior: Select a size no greater than the advertised value, measured in octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not select a compression table size greater than the advertised value.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoder's selected or signaled table size can be compared with the received limit.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH (0x02):  This setting can be used to enable or
      disable server push.  A server MUST NOT send a PUSH_PROMISE frame
      if it receives this parameter set to a value of 0; see
      Section 8.4.  A client that has both set this parameter to 0 and
      had it acknowledged MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE frame
      as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a server has received SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH set to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not send a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound server frames can be monitored after applying the setting value 0.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH (0x02):  This setting can be used to enable or
      disable server push.  A server MUST NOT send a PUSH_PROMISE frame
      if it receives this parameter set to a value of 0; see
      Section 8.4.  A client that has both set this parameter to 0 and
      had it acknowledged MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE frame
      as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a client has set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0, that setting has been acknowledged, and the client receives a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt of the PUSH_PROMISE as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can complete the setting acknowledgment sequence and inject PUSH_PROMISE to observe the error.

requirements.quote:
The initial value of SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH is 1.  For a client,
      this value indicates that it is willing to receive PUSH_PROMISE
      frames.  For a server, this initial value has no effect, and is
      equivalent to the value 0.  Any value other than 0 or 1 MUST be
      treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: Before a valid SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH value is received or otherwise applied.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an initial SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH value of 1; for a server, treat that initial value as having no effect and as equivalent to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial client and server setting state and resulting push behavior can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
The initial value of SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH is 1.  For a client,
      this value indicates that it is willing to receive PUSH_PROMISE
      frames.  For a server, this initial value has no effect, and is
      equivalent to the value 0.  Any value other than 0 or 1 MUST be
      treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH value other than 0 or 1 is received.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: An invalid setting value can be injected and the resulting connection error type observed.
